summary: A group of projects, programmes and other portfolios that your organisation chooses between and funds against its strategy.
example: Cooperative Investment Portfolio, which decides each season which of the quality, market access and member services work to fund first.
definition: A portfolio is a strategic investment and prioritisation construct: the projects, programmes and other portfolios an organisation selects, prioritises and oversees together against its strategic objectives (PMI, The Standard for Portfolio Management; MoP). What it holds need not depend on one another or share a benefit; what they share is the decision about which to fund. So it holds what is its own: the strategic objectives it is prioritised against, the budgets it allocates, the team that governs it, and its decisions (invest, hold or stop, in order), kept in a file beside it. What is in it says so itself. A portfolio is not a programme (related work coordinated to bring about one change, with a theory of change), not a project (work with a start and an end that produces outputs), and not a collection (a person's own grouping, which decides nothing). TAXONOMY.md D32.

cues.portfolio: a set of projects ranked and funded against the strategy

/metadata/name.guide: The portfolio's name, as people refer to it.

poor.why: Names what is in it today, not the investment decision it exists for.

/spec/aim.guide: What the portfolio invests in and to what end: the purpose its choices serve, in one sentence.
good: Fund the work that most raises what members earn from each season's produce.

poor.text: Coordinate the quality projects so they deliver one standard.
poor.why: That is a programme's aim: one change brought about by related work. A portfolio decides what to fund.

/spec/objectives.guide: The strategic objectives the portfolio is prioritised against: goals and objectives, never outcomes. Each thing it holds is judged by how far it advances these.

poor.why: An outcome: what is true once an objective is met. A portfolio serves what the organisation sets out to do.

/spec/leadTeam.guide: The team that governs the portfolio: it selects what goes in, sets the order, and decides what to invest in, hold or stop. A team, never a person.

/spec/funding.guide: The budgets the portfolio allocates. What it holds may also draw on budgets of its own.

/spec/reviewCycle.guide: How often the portfolio's decisions are reviewed, if on a fixed cycle.

/spec/portfolios.guide: The portfolios this one is part of, when portfolios nest: a regional portfolio inside the organisation's. Leave empty for a top-level portfolio.

Programme:/spec/portfolios.ask: Which programmes does this portfolio fund and prioritise? A programme names the portfolios it is in, so open each programme and choose this portfolio.
Programme:/spec/portfolios.ifNone: Define the portfolio first, then have each programme it funds name it. A programme it does not choose between stays outside it.

Project:/spec/alignment/portfolios.ask: Which projects does this portfolio fund and prioritise, outside any programme it holds? A project names the portfolios it is in, so open the project and choose this portfolio.
Project:/spec/alignment/portfolios.ifNone: Define the portfolio first, then have each project it chooses between name it.

Portfolio:/spec/portfolios.ask: Which portfolios sit inside this one? A portfolio names the portfolios it is part of.
Portfolio:/spec/portfolios.ifNone: Most portfolios hold no other portfolio. Nest one only when it is governed and decided on its own, inside this one.

checks.portfolio-objectives: Name the strategic objectives the portfolio is prioritised against.
checks.portfolio-holds: Have each project, programme or portfolio in it name this portfolio, from its own definition.
checks.portfolio-decided: Record a decision for each thing it holds, and only for those: invest, hold or stop, with a priority and a reason.
